subject: Platform fit + proposed evaluation plan for SkyTech (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@skytech.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Platform fit + proposed evaluation plan for SkyTech (post-discovery)

Alex — thanks again for the 45-minute sync today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before scheduling the technical deep-dive.

Summary from our call:
- Use case: conversational assistant + retrieval + tool access for internal analytics workflows (500–2,000 token contexts, heavy streaming UX).
- Current evaluation: SkyTech is comparing Redwood vs hyperscalers (AWS/GCP/Azure hosted inference) and a smaller self-hosted runtime for cost/latency.
- Must-haves called out: reliable streaming, robust function/tool-calling (typed inputs/outputs), deterministic structured outputs (JSON schema validation), and predictable unit economics for sustained throughput.

Redwood differentiators (high level):
- Streaming-first runtime with prefix/KV caching to keep tail latency low during interactive sessions.
- Native function/tool calling and typed structured output support (schema enforcement + validation hooks).
- Deployment flexibility: hosted API for quick POC, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) for procurement/regulatory requirements.
- Cost controls: batching, quantization recommendations, and routing policies to balance latency vs cost.

Proposed evaluation plan (what we recommend for a fair apples-to-apples run):
1) Streaming latency test — interactive scenario with 1k and 2k token contexts; measure time-to-first-byte and tail latency at 95/99th percentiles (goal: TTFB < 120ms at P95 for interactive traffic).
2) Function-calling accuracy run — execute our sample tool-calling harness (3 tools: search, small-table-lookup, execute-query) and validate fidelity to expected outputs.
3) Structured-output conformance — enforce JSON schema across 200 prompts and run automated validation; track failure modes and corrective prompts.
4) Throughput / cost simulation — run a 1-hour sustained batch at expected QPS to measure token cost and GPU utilization; compare to SkyTech’s hyperscaler results.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscalers-onepager.pdf (one-pager on differences), skytech-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (M-A-P with owners + timeline).

Immediate ask: please confirm interest in the above tests and share 2 windows next week for a 60–75 minute technical deep-dive with Marissa (SE) and me. If procurement wants early budget guidance, I can share a high-level cost estimate for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Thanks Soojin — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. We’re definitely interested in running those tests. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- On "streaming-first runtime": can you share a short script or curl-based harness we can run internally (we want reproducibility vs what our team ran on Vertex/AWS)?
- Procurement is asking for a very rough cost delta between Hosted and Private (order-of-magnitude is fine) so they can prioritize the procurement track.
- Is there any blocker to running the function-calling accuracy run on smaller instance sizes? We want to mimic production load but keep early costs low.

Available windows for the tech deep-dive: Tue 06/16 10:00–12:00 ET or Wed 06/17 14:00–16:00 ET. Let me know which works.

Alex — great, thanks for the quick reply. We can definitely provide everything you asked for: 
- I’ll have Marissa drop a curl/node/python harness (minimal deps) you can run end-to-end for streaming + function-calling. It will include a small script to measure TTFB and P95/P99.
- Cost delta: I’ll attach a 1-page hosted vs private order-of-magnitude note ahead of the deep-dive for procurement. High-level: Hosted is fastest to start (zero infra), Dedicated reduces per-token costs at scale with reserved capacity, Private adds platform fee + infra ops (often chosen for regulatory/ISV bundling). We’ll include a sample monthly cost ladder in the doc.
- Function-calling on smaller instances: yes — the runtime supports lower-SKU runs for validation; we’ll make recommendations for the test so the results remain meaningful to production expectations.

Proposed time: Tue 06/16 10:30–11:45 ET — works for Marissa and me. I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

One more ask for you: can you share a small representative prompt set (<=200 prompts) and an anonymized sample of the tool input shapes so we can pre-seed the harness? That will speed up the accuracy runs.
